diagnostic_evidence.quote: one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$

issues.failure_explanation: The statement requires a single y with all components bc_j(y,z) <= -zeta. Its negation only says that for each y SOME component satisfies bc_j(y,z^k) > -zeta_k, so the index j may depend on y. The proof instead fixes one j that works for every y in Y and for all k. That is a quantifier error, and the later steps (bc_j(.,z) >= 0 on all of Y, then a contradiction with one active constraint's MFCQ direction) depend on it. With vector-valued bc, the argument needs a different device. Examples are a minimax/convex-combination argument, or a pointwise construction of y_z with all components negative followed by a compactness (finite cover) argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the contradiction proof by a correct one. For each z in S, use MFCQ and continuity to build y_z in Y with bc(y_z,z)<0 in every component, treating inactive constraints by continuity. Then use continuity of bc in z and compactness of S to get a uniform zeta. Alternatively, use a minimax argument with multipliers mu in the simplex. The statement and downstream results stay unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform Slater constant zeta, and hence the multiplier bounds A and A_f, are not established by the given proof. The omega and alpha constants, the finite termination and rate of the SCP subsolver, the inner-solver guarantee in the outer method, and both complexity theorems rest on this bound.
issues.title: Uniform Slater property proved with an unjustified single constraint index in the contradiction argument
issues.why_classification: The theorem is true under the stated assumptions, and a contained, standard compactness or minimax argument repairs it. No downstream statement or constant changes, but the repair is more than a one-line fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $G_f < \infty$. Then it holds that

issues.failure_explanation: The constants omega_f, alpha_f and the bound on the inner iteration count K_{f,theta} depend on A_f, which is only established under the extra hypothesis G_f < infinity (Lemma lambda-uniform-bound). Assumption 1 does not give this: X = dom p may be unbounded, and ∇_y f(x,y) can be unbounded over X x Y, as for f(x,y)=xy with Y compact. Then A_f = infinity and the stated bound N_epsilon is meaningless. Theorem thm:operations lists only Assumptions 1 and 2 as hypotheses, so the hypothesis the proof needs is omitted.

failure_location.quote: the total number of evaluations of the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$, and the gradient $\nabla f$ performed by Algorithm~\ref{algo_implement:whole} is at most

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add G_f < infinity (for example, X bounded) to the hypotheses of Theorem thm:operations and to the corresponding statements in the introduction and remark. Alternatively, state the bound with the explicit dependence on A_f.
issues.overall_effect: The first-order oracle complexity bound, the paper's headline result, is not guaranteed under the stated assumptions. It is vacuous when G_f is infinite.
issues.title: Oracle-complexity theorem uses A_f without the needed hypothesis G_f < infinity
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis that the lemma already uses repairs it. The method, rates and scope are unchanged, and the numerical example has bounded domains.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, the constraint of~\eqref{surro_argmin} corresponds to the intersection of Euclidean balls.

issues.failure_explanation: The x-update minimizes a quadratic plus p over the ball B(x^k,r), and each SCP step minimizes a quadratic plus q over an intersection of m balls. These are prox-like problems for p + indicator(ball) and for q + indicator(ball intersection). Assumption 1(ii) only provides exact prox oracles for p and q themselves. The theorem counts each such subproblem as one proximal-operator evaluation of p or q, which is unsupported. Solving them in general needs extra inner work (for example, dual or multiplier iterations) not accounted for.

failure_location.quote: the total number of evaluations of the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$, and the gradient

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the counts as the number of solves of the ball-constrained subproblems (or assume a unit-cost oracle for them). Alternatively, bound the extra cost of solving them from p and q prox oracles.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bounds K_epsilon and N_epsilon on prox-oracle calls to p and q are not justified as proximal-operator counts. The count of gradient evaluations of f, which is the headline measure, is unaffected.
issues.title: Counts of 'proximal operator' evaluations ignore that the subproblems are constrained, not plain prox steps
issues.why_classification: Only the accounting of auxiliary oracle calls is affected. A reformulation of the claim or an added oracle assumption preserves all gradient-complexity guarantees and rates.
